recipes.name: Breezy Key Lime Pie with Strawberry Rhubarb Glaze

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Combine crumbs and butter in a bowl until evenly moistened; press into the bottom and up the sides of a 10-inch pie plate.
Beat sweetened condensed milk, Key lime zest, Key lime juice, egg yolks, and vanilla extract in a bowl with an electric mixer until smooth; pour filling into prepared crust.
Bake in the preheated oven until center is slightly jiggly, about 15 minutes. Cool for 10 minutes; refrigerate.

Combine rhubarb, strawberries, sugar, water, and pectin in a saucepan over medium heat; boil, stirring often, until rhubarb and berries break down and glaze begins to thicken and resemble jam, about 20 minutes. Cool until lukewarm; glaze will thicken as it cools.
Spread glaze over pie; refrigerate until chilled before serving, at least 8 hours for the best texture.

raw_recipe.description: This tasty breezy Key lime pie with strawberry rhubarb glaze recipe combines the tangy flavors of key lime with a bright strawberry-rhubarb glaze.

review.reviewBody: I have mixed feelings about this recipe, but as its first reviewer I’m happy to report that in the end it turned out delicious. First, 3 cups of crumbs was way off. I used half that and it worked out well. I also melted the butter, which I think made for easier mixing. The vanilla wafer crust was ok, but not as good as the traditional graham cracker crust. I also baked the crust for about 7 minutes before adding the filling. As for the filling, it’s a fairly standard Key lime pie filling, but with only 1 tsp. of lime zest I knew it would suffer some tartness and flavor, so I upped it to 1 T. and it proved to be just right. Since it is essentially double the typical amount of filling, I think it could have used another 5 minutes in the oven to fully set the filling. As for the glaze - vibrant, fruity flavor, pleasantly sweet and tart, with a vivid, ruby red color. I was torn between using it as a sauce rather than a glaze atop the whole pie and ultimately the decision was made for me. For whatever reason, the glaze didn’t gel as it should have, and never really thickened as it cooled. It would have never worked as a glaze. Maybe my fruit pectin was too old. But it was PERFECT as a sauce, and that’s really how I wanted it anyway! So as it turned out I was quite pleased that it “failed.” This is a beautiful, light, refreshing spring/summer pie. I broke my own rule by serving guests a recipe I’ve never tried before - and I lucked out.

I didn't make the pie, but I made the sauce for another dessert. It's has great balance of sweetness and tangy, and just the right consistency (runny enough to put in a squeeze bottle, but still with some body) to pour over ice cream or whatever you might want!
